title: What Comes After the Midterms
text:
Editor’s Note: Washington Week With The Atlantic is a partnership between NewsHour Productions, WETA, and The Atlantic airing every Friday on PBS stations nationwide. Check your local listings , watch full episodes here , or listen to the weekly podcast here . 

 What will Donald Trump do with the remaining two years of his presidency, and how will Democrats in Congress respond? On Washington Week With The Atlantic , panelists joined to discuss this and more.

 A Democrat-controlled Congress will soon have the chance to act on many of the issues that brought people out to vote, panelists explained last night. Issues such as the war in Iran, immigration, and the president’s use of the National Guard are among the “central touchpoints that we’ve seen over the last couple of years that have really driven people to anger, and to the polls,” Adam Harris, the host of Radio Atlantic , argued. And although some people will say that the results of the midterms are “retribution from Democrats,” he added, “a lot of voters will say it’s accountability.”

 Joining the editor in chief of The Atlantic , Jeffrey Goldberg, to discuss this and more: Peter Baker, a chief White House correspondent at The New York Times ; Leigh Ann Caldwell, a chief Washington correspondent at Puck ; Stephen Hayes, the editor and CEO of The Dispatch ; and Harris.
